name: Baniwa do Içana / Baniwa-Kuripako
confidence_why: Ramirez's 2001 reference grammar and dictionary give a near-exceptionless rule placing the pitch accent on the syllable before the last metrical syllable (never on the final syllable, with a dictionary-listed set of extrametrical suffixes that pushes surface accent to the antepenult or earlier), Taylor 1991 independently treats the penult as the unmarked position, and Souza 2012, the shorter master's thesis behind the 'variable' coding, reports the same penult-dominant surface spread without proposing a rule, so the reading is well supported even though only one description states the rule in full.

sweep_summary: bani1255 (Baniwa do Içana, catalog 'variable' from Souza 2012). The search of works with stress or accent in the title found only two Glottolog entries, both the same chapter: Mosonyi 2002 on 'baniva de Maroa, idioma tonal arawak del río Negro, Venezuela'. That is Baniva of Maroa/Guainía (ISO bvv = Glottolog bani1254, Venezuela), a different language: Glottolog's bib record links it to bwi by a 'computerized assignment' from the name 'Baniva', and Ramirez 2001:38 states explicitly that Baniwa-Curripaco is 'nitidamente' distinct from 'a outra língua, o Baniva de Maroa' (treated in his ch. 8; classified in the Alto Orinoco division with Yavitero). Both items: another language or variety, priority none for this language; no open copy exists (HathiTrust search-only, OCLC 50569122; archive.org 0 hits; volume reviews paywalled). Records saved and logged in Best first-hand statement read: Ramirez 2001 (already held by the project from our earlier reading), p. 46 and p. 89: pitch accent always on the syllable preceding the last metrical syllable, never final, with a dictionary-listed set of extrametrical suffixes, 'como uma língua de acento fixo' — this supersedes Souza 2012 and supports reclassification from 'variable' to fixed-dominant penult with listed-set suffix extrametricality, as our earlier reading already recommended. No new source changes that picture.

new_statements.quote: O sistema prosódico do Baniwa-Curripaco (dialeto central) é simples: o acento de altura cai sempre na sílaba que precede imediatamente a última sílaba métrica da palavra. Em outras palavras, o sistema prosódico é um sistema misto de acentuação lexical, com a existência de sufixos extramétricos (a metricidade de cada sufixo é dada pelo dicionário) e de acentuação pós-lexical (com o acento na sílaba que precede imediatamente a última sílaba métrica, como uma língua de acento fixo). [p. 89:] o acento nunca cai na última sílaba fonética da [palavra] fonológica. Ele cai sempre na sílaba que precede imediatamente a última sílaba métrica
new_statements.translation: The prosodic system of Baniwa-Curripaco (central dialect) is simple: the pitch accent always falls on the syllable immediately preceding the last metrical syllable of the word. In other words, the prosodic system is a mixed one, of lexical accentuation, with extrametrical suffixes (the metricality of each suffix is given by the dictionary), and post-lexical accentuation (with the accent on the syllable immediately preceding the last metrical syllable, like a fixed-accent language). [p. 89:] the accent never falls on the last phonetic syllable of the phonological word. It always falls on the syllable immediately preceding the last metrical syllable.
new_statements.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: Editora da Universidade do Amazonas (EDUA). 798 pp. Ch. 2 'Baniwa-Curripaco e Tariano'.

new_statements.reading: Pitch accent on the penultimate metrical syllable of the phonological word, never on the final syllable; surface antepenultimate (and earlier) accents are the same penult rule applied over a closed, dictionary-listed set of extrametrical outer suffixes (all object person markers, -ka subordinator, -nai plural, etc.). Ramirez himself calls it 'como uma língua de acento fixo' with lexical extrametricality. This is a fixed: penultimate syllable (right-edge, morphologically conditioned extrametricality) system, not free/variable stress; the H vs LH melody contrast on heavy tonic syllables (pp. 93-94) is a separate pitch accent contrast matching the catalog's the secondary-stress rule. Ramirez's 'dialeto central' = Baniwa do Içana = bani1255. Text-layer scanned shows '111' for 'm' and 'ela' for 'da'; quote normalised accordingly.

new_statements.quote: O acento tônico nunca cai na última sílaba. No dialeto central, ele cai sempre na sílaba que precede imediatamente a última sílaba métrica da palavra (regra de assinalação do acento). Para colocá-lo corretamente, basta saber qual é o comportamento tônico dos sufixos da língua. Um sufixo pode ser: – ou métrico: ele obedece então à regra de assinalação do acento. – ou extramétrico: ele é então «transparente» e não conta na regra de assinalação do acento. [...] 5. No caso das vogais longas, o acento pode cair na 1ª ou na 2ª parte da vogal. Treine bem: TOM ALTO kéetto capivara / TOM ASCENDENTE keétto certa formiga
new_statements.translation: Word stress never falls on the last syllable. In the central dialect it always falls on the syllable immediately preceding the last metrical syllable of the word (stress-assignment rule). To place it correctly it suffices to know the stress behaviour of the language's suffixes. A suffix can be either metrical: it then obeys the stress-assignment rule; or extrametrical: it is then 'transparent' and does not count in the stress-assignment rule. [...] 5. In the case of long vowels, the stress can fall on the 1st or the 2nd part of the vowel. Practise: HIGH TONE kéetto capybara / RISING TONE keétto a certain ant. (scanned in the text layer garbled 'que' as 'tJUC', 'é' as 'e', 'assinalação' as 'ass in alação', 'ALTO' as 't\LTO'; normalised here against the printed page.)

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement and same analysis as the existing statement from Ramirez's 2001 grammar (Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional, sec. 2.1.1 point 10 / 2.1.5.1): penultimate metrical syllable, never final, with lexically extrametrical suffixes and a high-vs-rising melody contrast on long tonic vowels. It refines the record only in that the dictionary itself is the source of the per-suffix metricity list and states that all object / adjective-subject person suffixes are extrametrical. The catalog record for bani1255 has an empty rule field; this work supports filling it as penultimate (metrical) syllable with extrametrical suffixes.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress on the penultimate metrical syllable of the word, never on the final syllable; each suffix is lexically metrical (counts) or extrametrical (transparent), so surface antepenultimate stress arises when an extrametrical suffix (e.g. progressive -ka, all object / adjective-subject person suffixes) closes the word (nokápa 'I see' > nokápaka 'I am seeing' vs metrical -de: nokapáde 'I always see'). The dictionary marks the metricity of every suffix. On a stressed long vowel the accent sits on the first or the second mora, giving a lexical high vs rising melody contrast (kéetto vs keétto); nasal vowels are always long with rising tone.
new_statements.exceptions: Extrametrical suffixes are the only source of non-penult surface stress; the rule is stated for the central dialect only ('No dialeto central'), leaving open that the northern (curripaco) and southern superdialects differ, which the dictionary does not describe. Long-vowel tonic syllables carry either high or rising melody (a lexical contrast, listed in alphabetical order high before rising, p. 8).
new_statements.identity_note: The dictionary's reference variety is the Super-dialeto Central of baniwa-curripaco, 'especialmente o que se escuta no rio Içana, perto da foz do rio Aiari' (Introdução, printed p. 3, p. 8), i.e. Baniwa do Içana proper = bani1255. Ramirez explicitly separates it from Baniva de Maroa (rio Guainía, Venezuela; bani1254/bvv), and the stress rule is stated for the central dialect only; the northern (curripaco) and southern (Victorino) superdialects are lexically annotated in the entries but their accent placement is not described.

tone_statements.citation: Cronhamn, Sandra. 2025. A grammar of Baniwa classifiers. Doctoral thesis (monograph), Centre for Languages and Literature, Lund University. 329 pp. ISBN 978-91-89874-69-5 (print), 978-91-89874-70-1 (pdf).
tone_statements.quote: Instead, stress is marked by pitch, i.e., the stressed syllable in a phonological word is the syllable with the highest pitch (Ramirez, 2020a: 92). ... When stress falls on a light syllable (i.e., a short vowel), it always receives high tone (Ramirez, 2020a: 81). When stress falls on a heavy syllable, that is, a bimoraic one (a long vowel or a diphthong), the high tone can dock on either mora. This is distinguished phonetically as a high tone (/V́V/, [´]) and a rising contour tone (/VV́/, [ˇ]), as shown in the minimal pair kéetto [ké:t̪o] 'capybara' and keétto [kě:t̪o] 'ant sp.' (Ramirez, 2020a: 95). Tone is an inherent lexical property.
tone_statements.summary: Word stress fixed on the penultimate metric syllable (extrametric suffixes lexically listed), cued by pitch only; a two-way tonal contrast H vs LH (rising) confined to stressed heavy (bimoraic) syllables, described as an inherent lexical property; light stressed syllables always H; suffix classes (centripetal vs centrifugal) determine which mora of a preceding heavy syllable carries the H.

tone_statements.citation: Apolinário, Valkiria. 2020. Estudo de aspectos fonológicos do Baníwa (Aruák) do médio Içana, por uma falante nativa. Dissertação (Mestrado em Linguística), Universidade de Brasília (orient. Ana Suelly Arruda Câmara Cabral). 72 f.
tone_statements.quote: Existen tres acentos tonales fundamentales (conocemos por lo menos dos más, de poca ocurrencia), en cierta forma análogos a los que presentan el sueco y el noruego ... El agudo (´) indica que la sílaba acentuada se pronuncia en un nivel alto y con bastante fuerza espiratoria ... Con el acento grave (`) la sílaba acentuada se pronuncia fuerte y en un nivel bajo ... El tercer acento, llamado circunflejo (^), indica que la sílaba acentuada, siempre intensa, es alta y las inacentuadas, débiles, se desplazan al nivel medio o incluso bajo
tone_statements.translation: There are three fundamental tonal accents (we know of at least two more, of low occurrence), in a way analogous to those of Swedish and Norwegian ... The acute (´) indicates that the accented syllable is pronounced at a high level and with considerable expiratory force ... With the grave accent (`) the accented syllable is pronounced strong and at a low level ... The third accent, called circumflex (^), indicates that the accented syllable, always intense, is high and the unaccented ones, weak, move to the mid or even low level
tone_statements.locator: p. 130 ('Existen tres acentos tonales..') and p. 131 (circunflejo examples continue p. 132); no section numbering
tone_statements.summary: Baniva of Maroa (Venezuela), not Baniwa of Içana: three tonal accents (acute, grave, circumflex) like Swedish, plus two rare ones; pitch subordinate to stress; present-day speakers keep stress only.

tone_statements.citation: Crevels, M. et al. (2002). La fonologia suprasegmental y otras particularidades del baniva de Maroa, idioma tonal arawak del Rio Negro, Venezuela. In Current Studies on South American Languages.
tone_statements.quote: Baniwa-Hohodene, em nível superficial fonético, é uma língua acentual e não tonal, estando, provavelmente, em um processo de transição de um sistema de acento de altura ("pitch accent") para um sistema de acento de intensidade ("stress accent"), ou seja, um processo de "tonotanásia", devido, possivelmente, ao contato dos falantes da comunidade Ucuki-Cachoeira com o português ... a proeminência acentual é um fenômeno pluriparamétrico, com uma predominância maior da freqüência fundamental, uma vez que está sempre em uma sílaba alta da palavra
tone_statements.translation: Baniwa-Hohodene, at the surface phonetic level, is an accentual and not a tonal language, probably in a process of transition from a pitch-accent system to a stress-accent system, i.e. a process of "tonothanasia", possibly due to the contact of the speakers of the Ucuki-Cachoeira community with Portuguese ... the accentual prominence is a multi-parameter phenomenon, with a greater predominance of fundamental frequency, since it is always on a high syllable of the word
tone_statements.locator: Conclusão final, points 1-2 (and point 6, footnote 1), p. 183; typology of tonal vs accentual (pitch accent / stress accent) languages in cap. 1 §1.2.3 'Considerações terminológicas', p. 22; hypotheses a-b in §1.1.1, p. 14
tone_statements.summary: Acoustic-perceptual study: Baniwa-Hohodene is accentual, not tonal; one free word accent, mostly penultimate, cued chiefly by F0 (pitch accent probably drifting toward stress accent).

tone_statements.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: Editora da Universidade do Amazonas. 798 pp. ISBN 85-7401-084-7. (ch. 2 Baniwa-Curripaco e Tariano)
tone_statements.quote: Quando as regras de assinalamento do acento leva111-no a cair numa sílaba foneticamente pesada (V longa ou ditongo). duas realizações fonéticas em oposição são possíveis: uma com tom de registro alto ou (como variante livre) com tom de contorno descendente: outra. com tom ele contorno ascendente. ... Esta oposição tonal parece ser de tipo lexical e é dada pelo dicionário. ... Isso nos permite interpretar, em subjacente, o Baniwa-Curripaco como urna língua de« pitch-accent »e não como uma língua tonal.
tone_statements.translation: When the accent-assignment rules make it fall on a phonetically heavy syllable (long V or diphthong), two phonetic realisations in opposition are possible: one with a high register tone or (as a free variant) with a falling contour tone; the other with a rising contour tone. ... This tonal opposition seems to be of lexical type and is given by the dictionary. ... This allows us to interpret Baniwa-Curripaco, underlyingly, as a 'pitch-accent' language and not as a tone language.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 93-94, sec. 2.1.5.3 'As melodias alta e ascendente'; inventory also stated at sec. 2.1.3.2 p. 76; 2.1.1 phoneme list p. 43 and p. 45; accent = 'acento de altura' p. 88.
tone_statements.summary: pitch accent, expressly not a tone language: one high-pitched accented syllable per word; on long vowels/diphthongs two lexical melodies contrast, high (or falling) vs rising (accent on mora 1 vs 2).

tone_statements.citation: França, Maria Cristina Victorino de. 1993. Fonologia Sincrônica e Diacrônica do Baníwa-Siusi: um tratamento não-linear. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina, Florianópolis. 138 pp.
tone_statements.quote: A nível subjacente morfolexical, o sistema nSo é acentuai 'pitch' mas sim tonal ... 0 sistema tonal subjacente é simples e resulta das seguintes associaçSes de auto-segmentos tonais: (a) um tom alto associa-se sempre ao núcleo da primeira sílaba dos morfemas lexicais nominais ou verbais; <b) um tom alto associa-se ao núcleo silábico de certos morfemas gramaticais que constituem uma lista fechada; (c) um tom baixo associa-se a todos os núcleos silábicos dos morfemas lexicais ou gramaticais que nSo receberam um tom alto.
tone_statements.translation: At the underlying morpholexical level the system is not a 'pitch' accentual one but tonal ... The underlying tonal system is simple and results from the following associations of tonal autosegments: (a) a high tone always associates to the nucleus of the first syllable of nominal or verbal lexical morphemes; (b) a high tone associates to the syllable nucleus of certain grammatical morphemes that form a closed list; (c) a low tone associates to all syllable nuclei of lexical or grammatical morphemes that did not receive a high tone.
tone_statements.locator: p. 49, sec. 2.2.4 'Sistema tonal subjacente' (section begins p. 48)
tone_statements.summary: Underlyingly tonal: high vs low on syllable nuclei, high on root-initial syllables and on a closed list of grammatical morphemes; lowering rules leave one high per word, realised as a pitch accent.

audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant penultimate (right edge; penultimate stress counting metrical syllables), exceptions = listed-set of lexically extrametrical suffixes (outer inflectional suffixes incl. all object markers, -ka SUB, -nai PL; ~100 suffixes each classified in the dictionary), final syllable never stressed; keep the secondary-stress rule (H vs LH pitch accent contrast on heavy tonic syllables, Ramirez 2001:93-94 = Souza 2012:189). If house convention files affix-extrametricality systems under 'morphological' (cf. yuhu1238), use that instead; either way not 'variable'. Deciding quote: Ramirez 2001:46 and 89 ('o acento.. cai sempre na sílaba que precede imediatamente a última sílaba métrica da palavra.. como uma língua de acento fixo').
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the Souza 2012 passage is verbatim in the PDF we hold at pp. 188-189 as cited. (2) The classification 'variable, no positional rule' faithfully reflects Souza 2012, but Souza is an MA segmental phonology that treats accent in 6 pages, finds no stress minimal pairs in its own corpus, and defers ('é necessário um aprofundamento maior'). The reference grammar of record, Ramirez 2001 (Glottolog's top-ranked grammar, 798 pp, now downloaded from the author-shared open copy), states an explicit and near-exceptionless rule: pitch accent on the syllable immediately preceding the last metrical syllable; never final; suffixes are lexically metrical or extrametrical (listed in the dictionary), so surface antepenult/pre-antepenult accents are the penult rule applied over transparent outer suffixes; Ramirez himself calls it 'como uma língua de acento fixo' combined with lexical extrametrica

tone.quote: Quando as regras de assinalamento do acento leva111-no a cair numa sílaba foneticamente pesada (V longa ou ditongo). duas realizações fonéticas em oposição são possíveis: uma com tom de registro alto ou (como variante livre) com tom de contorno descendente: outra. com tom ele contorno ascendente. ... Esta oposição tonal parece ser de tipo lexical e é dada pelo dicionário. ... Isso nos permite interpretar, em subjacente, o Baniwa-Curripaco como urna língua de« pitch-accent »e não como uma língua tonal.
tone.locator: pp. 93-94, sec. 2.1.5.3 'As melodias alta e ascendente'; inventory also stated at sec. 2.1.3.2 p. 76; 2.1.1 phoneme list p. 43 and p. 45; accent = 'acento de altura' p. 88.
tone.translation: When the accent-assignment rules make it fall on a phonetically heavy syllable (long V or diphthong), two phonetic realisations in opposition are possible: one with a high register tone or (as a free variant) with a falling contour tone; the other with a rising contour tone. ... This tonal opposition seems to be of lexical type and is given by the dictionary. ... This allows us to interpret Baniwa-Curripaco, underlyingly, as a 'pitch-accent' language and not as a tone language.
tone.summary: pitch accent, expressly not a tone language: one high-pitched accented syllable per word; on long vowels/diphthongs two lexical melodies contrast, high (or falling) vs rising (accent on mora 1 vs 2).
tone.says: pitch accent, expressly not a tone language: one high-pitched accented syllable per word; on long vowels/diphthongs two lexical melodies contrast, high (or falling) vs rising (accent on mora 1 vs 2).

sources.quote: 'O acento tônico em baniwa é essencialmente a pronúncia mais alta de uma das sílabas de uma palavra ... O acento é distintivo: píipiri "pupunha" / pipíiri "você envia" ... No sistema gráfico adotado aqui, o acento "normal" não marcado cai na penúltima sílaba ... Se o acento não cai na penúltima sílaba, é marcado na grafia: hámuri "ano", iaká "longe"'; object pronouns subordinate to the accent of the verb complex (rikápa-hnuà); author calls accent 'um dos aspectos mais complexos da análise do baniwa' and gives no rule beyond the penult default.

sources.quote: Instead, stress is marked by pitch, i.e., the stressed syllable in a phonological word is the syllable with the highest pitch (Ramirez, 2020a: 92). ... When stress falls on a light syllable (i.e., a short vowel), it always receives high tone (Ramirez, 2020a: 81). When stress falls on a heavy syllable, that is, a bimoraic one (a long vowel or a diphthong), the high tone can dock on either mora. This is distinguished phonetically as a high tone (/V́V/, [´]) and a rising contour tone (/VV́/, [ˇ]), as shown in the minimal pair kéetto [ké:t̪o] 'capybara' and keétto [kě:t̪o] 'ant sp.' (Ramirez, 2020a: 95). Tone is an inherent lexical property.
sources.note: Sec. 3.1.2 'Suprasegmental phonology' (pp. 62-63): stress on the penultimate METRIC syllable (suffixes lexically metric/extrametric), stress realised by pitch not intensity/duration; sec. 3.1.2.3 'Tone': stressed light syllable = H; on a stressed heavy (bimoraic) syllable H docks on either mora giving a lexical contrast high /V́V/ vs rising /VV́/ (kéetto 'capybara' vs keétto 'ant sp.'); metric suffixes split into centripetal (rising on preceding heavy syllable) vs centrifugal (high), offered as a historical source of the tone contrast (all after Ramirez 2020a).

tone.summary: Word stress fixed on the penultimate metric syllable (extrametric suffixes lexically listed), cued by pitch only; a two-way tonal contrast H vs LH (rising) confined to stressed heavy (bimoraic) syllables, described as an inherent lexical property; light stressed syllables always H; suffix classes (centripetal vs centrifugal) determine which mora of a preceding heavy syllable carries the H.

tone.translation: There are three fundamental tonal accents (we know of at least two more, of low occurrence), in a way analogous to those of Swedish and Norwegian ... The acute (´) indicates that the accented syllable is pronounced at a high level and with considerable expiratory force ... With the grave accent (`) the accented syllable is pronounced strong and at a low level ... The third accent, called circumflex (^), indicates that the accented syllable, always intense, is high and the unaccented ones, weak, move to the mid or even low level
tone.summary: Baniva of Maroa (Venezuela), not Baniwa of Içana: three tonal accents (acute, grave, circumflex) like Swedish, plus two rare ones; pitch subordinate to stress; present-day speakers keep stress only.

tone.quote: A nível subjacente morfolexical, o sistema nSo é acentuai 'pitch' mas sim tonal ... 0 sistema tonal subjacente é simples e resulta das seguintes associaçSes de auto-segmentos tonais: (a) um tom alto associa-se sempre ao núcleo da primeira sílaba dos morfemas lexicais nominais ou verbais; <b) um tom alto associa-se ao núcleo silábico de certos morfemas gramaticais que constituem uma lista fechada; (c) um tom baixo associa-se a todos os núcleos silábicos dos morfemas lexicais ou gramaticais que nSo receberam um tom alto.
tone.locator: p. 49, sec. 2.2.4 'Sistema tonal subjacente' (section begins p. 48)
tone.translation: At the underlying morpholexical level the system is not a 'pitch' accentual one but tonal ... The underlying tonal system is simple and results from the following associations of tonal autosegments: (a) a high tone always associates to the nucleus of the first syllable of nominal or verbal lexical morphemes; (b) a high tone associates to the syllable nucleus of certain grammatical morphemes that form a closed list; (c) a low tone associates to all syllable nuclei of lexical or grammatical morphemes that did not receive a high tone.
tone.summary: Underlyingly tonal: high vs low on syllable nuclei, high on root-initial syllables and on a closed list of grammatical morphemes; lowering rules leave one high per word, realised as a pitch accent.
tone.says: Underlyingly tonal: high vs low on syllable nuclei, high on root-initial syllables and on a closed list of grammatical morphemes; lowering rules leave one high per word, realised as a pitch accent.

tone.quote: Baniwa-Hohodene, em nível superficial fonético, é uma língua acentual e não tonal, estando, provavelmente, em um processo de transição de um sistema de acento de altura ("pitch accent") para um sistema de acento de intensidade ("stress accent"), ou seja, um processo de "tonotanásia", devido, possivelmente, ao contato dos falantes da comunidade Ucuki-Cachoeira com o português ... a proeminência acentual é um fenômeno pluriparamétrico, com uma predominância maior da freqüência fundamental, uma vez que está sempre em uma sílaba alta da palavra
tone.locator: Conclusão final, points 1-2 (and point 6, footnote 1), p. 183; typology of tonal vs accentual (pitch accent / stress accent) languages in cap. 1 §1.2.3 'Considerações terminológicas', p. 22; hypotheses a-b in §1.1.1, p. 14
tone.translation: Baniwa-Hohodene, at the surface phonetic level, is an accentual and not a tonal language, probably in a process of transition from a pitch-accent system to a stress-accent system, i.e. a process of "tonothanasia", possibly due to the contact of the speakers of the Ucuki-Cachoeira community with Portuguese ... the accentual prominence is a multi-parameter phenomenon, with a greater predominance of fundamental frequency, since it is always on a high syllable of the word
tone.summary: Acoustic-perceptual study: Baniwa-Hohodene is accentual, not tonal; one free word accent, mostly penultimate, cued chiefly by F0 (pitch accent probably drifting toward stress accent).
tone.says: Acoustic-perceptual study: Baniwa-Hohodene is accentual, not tonal; one free word accent, mostly penultimate, cued chiefly by F0 (pitch accent probably drifting toward stress accent).
